elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered text opens "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ... EXCEED", replacing "TRUELINK'S", so the ceiling now binds Client and TrueLink alike.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The retained basis is "TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 floor, no "greater of" construct, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and the 12 months are not anchored to the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The edited sentence contains no exclusion of indirect, consequential, special or incidental damages for either party, and no such language is cited elsewhere.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out reads "OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list names only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct; data protection and security obligations remain inside the cap.
"OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ... WHICH ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION" places the Section 12a indemnity outside the ceiling for both parties.
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" appears in the carve-out and is now stated as "A PARTY'S", so it is mutual rather than TrueLink-only.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" is carved out of the limitation for either party.
No fraud carve-out was added to the parenthetical.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears; only the indemnity route (if the indemnity covers IP) sits outside the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing states that Client's obligation to pay hosting/support compensation is not "damages" for cap purposes; the mutualised cap could now be argued to limit Client's payment liability.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY FOR ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT ... EXCEED ..." — one-sided TrueLink-only cap is cured; note the clause is per-"matter" rather than expressly "aggregate", which is retained original phrasing.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained "TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD"; hosting and support services are the compensated deliverables under this hosting agreement, so the 12-month fee basis is real rather than illusory (any non-hosting/support fee streams would sit outside the basis and should be checked).
Express carve-out for "A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS" stated as "NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Express carve-out for "BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS".
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative wording: cap mutualised ("EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY"), 12-month hosting-and-support fee basis retained, and indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly "NOT SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION" for both parties.

Minimality fails: the redline also deleted "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" and substituted the Agreement as a whole. Cap scope is not an element of the chosen fallback, and the deletion strips a Customer-favourable restriction — under the original, TrueLink's liability outside those sections was uncapped, whereas the edit now caps TrueLink across the entire Agreement. Repair by restoring the existing scope words (e.g. "ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11 OF THIS AGREEMENT") and, if the drafter genuinely believes Sections 3, 4 and 11 do not exist, raise that as a separate cross-reference correction rather than folding a scope expansion into the LOL-CAP redline.

Preferred level remains open (correctly not pursued): no USD 1,000,000 "greater of" floor, no "paid or payable", no anchoring of the 12 months to the event giving rise to the claim, no mutual indirect/consequential damages exclusion, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or IP infringement.

Preferred-level payment carve-out is absent and now carries added risk: because the cap has been made mutual, Client's obligation to pay hosting and support compensation could be argued to fall under the ceiling. Add "Nothing in this Section limits Client's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement." if the team escalates to the preferred position.

Intent preserved: no new undefined terms are introduced and the amended sentence is internally consistent; the only interpretive change flagged above is the enlarged cap scope, which the indemnification carve-out partly mitigates.
